scope_justification: Agent Autofill provides user-directed email productivity through a local broker. An authorized agent can search and read messages in a user-selected Gmail label or retrieve a recent sign-in code for an exact recipient and task. Message-body access is required; gmail.metadata cannot supply bodies. The app does not send, modify, or delete email, so gmail.modify and mail.google.com are unnecessary. OAuth credentials remain in the operating-system credential store. The broker enforces authenticated task permissions before returning selected data. An external acting agent may transmit returned content to its model provider; the homepage and privacy policy disclose this data flow.
data_flow: The user supplies a Desktop OAuth client and authorizes Gmail in Google's browser consent flow.
A temporary loopback listener receives the authorization code; state and PKCE protect the exchange.
Client and refresh state remain in the operating-system credential store. Access tokens remain in process memory.
The Gmail API adapter checks account identity and the configured label, then issues read-only GET requests.
The broker applies its authenticated task access policy before returning selected information to the acting agent.

An external agent may transmit returned content to its model provider. Reviewer materials must disclose this and the provider configuration; do not claim all processing stays on device or assume an assessment exemption.
